prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help you find the right lawyer — first I need a few details so my recommendations are useful. Meanwhile here’s practical guidance you can use right now.

Quick questions
- When did the accident happen?
- Where exactly in/near Pleasanton (intersection or freeway)?
- Were there serious injuries (hospitalized, surgery, ongoing treatment)?
- Who was at fault (other driver, commercial vehicle, government vehicle)?
- Have you given a recorded statement to an insurance company or signed any releases?
- Do you want to pursue a settlement or are you prepared for trial?
- Any preference on lawyer type (big firm vs. local solo, language needs, budget)?

Important deadlines (act fast)
- Standard personal-injury statute of limitations in California: 2 years from the date of injury.
- If the claim is against a public entity (city, county, transit agency), you usually must file a government claim within a much shorter period (often 6 months). Get a lawyer immediately if a government agency is involved.

Immediate steps to take
1. Seek and continue medical care — document everything.
2. Preserve evidence: photos of vehicles, injuries, scene; police report number; witness names/contacts; repair estimates.
3. Don’t give recorded statements to the other party’s insurer or sign releases without talking to a lawyer.
4. Keep a pain/injury journal and copies of all medical bills, wage loss documentation, and communications with insurers.
5. Get a copy of the police report.

How to choose the right Pleasanton / Bay Area car-accident lawyer
Look for:
- Specialization in car accident / personal injury (not family law, etc.)
- Experience with your injury type and similar cases
- Trial experience and a track record of settlements/verdicts
- Clear contingency-fee terms (typical: ~33% for pre-suit, 33–40% thereafter) and whether they advance costs
- Good communication: who handles your case day-to-day, how often you’ll get updates
- Local courtroom experience in Alameda County / Tri-Valley area
- Positive client reviews and references; clean State Bar record

Questions to ask in the free consultation
- How many car-accident cases have you handled? How many went to trial?
- What similar cases have you settled and for how much (approximate ranges)?
- What is your contingency fee and what costs will I be responsible for up front or later?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day? How often will I hear from you?
- Do you advance medical/expert costs? How are medical liens handled?
- What’s a realistic timeline and likely value range for my case?
- Are you licensed in California and in good standing with the State Bar?

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific settlement amount.
- Pushy “sign now” tactics.
- Inability or unwillingness to put fee structure in writing.
- Poor responsiveness in the consultation phase.

Where to look for attorneys
- Alameda County Bar Association lawyer referral service
- California State Bar’s website (verify licensing/discipline)
- Reviews on Google, Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, or Super Lawyers
- Local recommendations (friends, coworkers, medical providers)

If you want, I can:
- Help evaluate specific attorneys or firms if you give me their names or links to profiles/reviews.
- Draft an email or phone script you can use in consultations.
- Help you prioritize options based on seriousness of injury or whether a government defendant was involved.

Tell me the answers to the quick questions above or give me a few lawyer names you’re considering and I’ll help you pick.
